intro: Exponential backoff reduces repeated pressure after failed requests. A cap prevents the wait between later retries from increasing without bound.
task: Generate capped exponential delays and total elapsed delay from attempt count.
requirements: retries is an integer 0..60; base and cap are finite nonnegative numbers. Return delays[i]=min(cap,base*2**i) for retry indices starting at zero, and total=sum(delays). cap may be below base. These are waiting delays, not request execution times.

Numeric values are finite Python ints or floats with magnitude at most 1e9; bool is not numeric. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: The first retry uses the base delay, so the exponent starts at zero.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Apply the cap to every delay before computing the total.

explanation: Exponential backoff reduces repeated pressure after failed requests. A cap prevents the wait between later retries from increasing without bound.
This deterministic schedule omits jitter and request duration. Keeping those concerns separate makes the delay budget easy to verify and compose with a real retry system.
